The only coverage is indirect, from the regenerated appState snapshots. — fix: Create the file with the 10 tests listed under U25 in change_plan.md. Render <Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally />, build elements with API.createElement/setElements/setSelectedElements, click controls with fireEvent on queryByTestId, use restoreElements/restoreAppState from ../data/restore and exportScene({type:'svg'}) from ../scene/export. Include the 'no arrowheadSize key when currentItemArrowheadSize is null' and 'no-field arrow equals today's restore output' assertions.
2. Earlier attempts at this file failed on these points; avoid each. (1) Never assert whole elements or inline snapshots of elements (fractional `index`, `id`, `seed`, `version` differ): assert only `arrowheadSize` and the fields under test. (2) Undo/redo is `Keyboard.undo()` / `Keyboard.redo()` (class Keyboard, tests/helpers/ui.ts:65,136), not `UI.undo`. (3) Paste styles: `API.executeAction(actionCopyStyles)` then select the target and `API.executeAction(actionPasteStyles)`, imported from "../actions/actionStyles" (tests/stickyNotes.test.tsx:36,251-253). (4) Flip: `API.executeAction(actionFlipHorizontal)` from "../actions/actionFlip", not a label click. (5) SVG export: the whole arrow path is dominated by the shaft (an earlier attempt compared 91.41 to 91.41); compare the head only, e.g. the extent of the arrow's head <path> (the path after the shaft in the arrow's <g>), or compare getArrowheadPoints of the two elements. (6) Every import must be used (eslint --max-warnings=0 failed on an unused `actionChangeArrowheadSize` import). (7) 'new arrows take the current size' must set `currentItemArrowheadSize` through the action or `API.setAppState` before drawing, and assert `"arrowheadSize" in el` is false only when the current size is null. Keep the file short (an earlier Opus attempt timed out at 540 s): about 10 focused tests, the U25 list in the plan. Answer with exactly one JSON object {path, content}.

instruction:
Fix `packages/element/tests/arrowheadSize.test.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. major: Only the default branch (triangle) of the new ~170-line getLinearElementRotatedBoundsWithHeads helper in bounds.ts is tested. No test runs the cardinality_one_or_many, cardinality_exactly_one, cardinality_zero_or_one and cardinality_zero_or_many decompositions, the circle/circle_outline radius path, the cardinality_one bar-only index-2 path, a start head, or a rotated arrow (the transformXY path). If any part offset or flag is wrong, the large-head bounds will be wrong and nothing will catch it. — fix: Add one parametrised 'large heads widen bounds' case per head type (circle, circle_outline, cardinality_one, the four composite cardinality markers, and a start head). Each should assert the bounds contain every drawn part's points (for circles, center ± diameter*scale/2). Also add one case with angle != 0 that checks containment against the rotated head points.
2. minor (line 1): This breaks the plan's test conventions: describe/expect/it are imported from 'vitest' although they are globals here, and '@excalidraw/common' is imported in two separate statements (lines 2 and 3-7). It also duplicates code: createStraightArrow is defined twice (in 'head points geometry' and in 'element bounds and hit testing'), and 'no field and medium give today's head points' repeats three near-identical API.createElement literals. — fix: Drop the vitest import and merge the two @excalidraw/common imports into one. Hoist a single createStraightArrow(arrowheadSize?, endArrowhead = 'triangle', points?) helper to the top-level describe and reuse it everywhere.
3. minor: The line case in 'small, medium and lines keep today's bounds' uses a line with no heads. The guarantee under test is that lines never widen bounds because shape.ts draws no heads for them, but the test never checks this for a line that actually has a head. The getElementBounds guard (isArrowElement) is therefore only weakly exercised. — fix: Create the large line with newLinearElement plus newElementWith(line, { endArrowhead: 'arrow', arrowheadSize: 'large' }), or extend API.createElement to accept arrowheads for lines. Then assert its bounds equal those of the same line without the size.
